earnings.title: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
highlights: For the quarter, revenue was $3.5 billion, income from railway operations was $1.2 billion, operating ratio was 67.4%, and diluted earnings per share were $3.37.

Adjusting the results to exclude merger-related expenses and the effects of the Eastern Ohio incident, third quarter income from railway operations was $1.2 billion, the operating ratio was 65.4%, and diluted earnings per share were $3.62.
Diluted earnings per share were $3.37, up $0.21, or 7%, compared to third quarter 2025.

Railway operating revenues of $3.5 billion were a quarterly record, up $423 million, or 14% compared to the third quarter 2025, on a volume increase of 3% year-over-year, and higher fuel surcharges representing eight points of the revenue growth .

quotes.text: Norfolk Southern delivered another quarter of solid execution, with record revenues, and strong earnings growth aided by continued productivity gains across the network, reflecting continued momentum in our business and the dedication of our team.
quotes.by: Mark George, Norfolk Southern President and Chief Executive Officer

items.heading: The Mergers are subject to conditions, some or all of which may not be satisfied or completed on a timely basis, if at all. Failure to complete the Mergers could have material adverse effects on the Company.
The Company is subject to business uncertainties and contractual restrictions while the Mergers are pending, which could adversely affect the Company’s business and operations.

Uncertainties associated with the Mergers may cause a loss of management personnel and other key employees, and the Company may have difficulty attracting and motivating management personnel and other key employees.

The costs, liabilities, fines, penalties, and/or financial impact resulting from or related to the Incident or the Incident Proceedings have been significant to date, may exceed expected or accrued amounts, and have and can be expected to continue to negatively affect our financial results.

New or additional governmental regulation and/or operational changes resulting from or related to the Incident or the Incident Proceedings may negatively impact us, our customers, the rail industry, or the markets we serve.

Governmental legislation, regulation, and Executive Orders over commercial, operational, tax, safety, security, or cybersecurity matters could negatively affect us, our customers, the rail industry, or the markets we serve.
